plan.chapterName: OpenStax Organic Chemistry, chapter 28: Biomolecules: Nucleic Acids
plan.contextChunk: This figure diagrams RNA transcription as a flat schematic of three nucleic acid strands drawn as tapered colored ribbons. A blue-violet ribbon runs across the top, labeled "DNA sense strand", marked 5' at its left tip and 3' at its right; a cyan ribbon runs along the bottom, labeled "DNA antisense strand", marked 3' at left and 5' at right. Both ribbons bow away from each other through the middle of the figure to open a bubble, and outside the bubble at each end their bases pair through vertical dot columns, C with G, A with T, and T with A at the left, G with C, A with T, and C with G at the right. Inside the bubble the sense strand's bases hang free and read T C A G C T G G C T G A A C G C G T T, while the antisense strand's exposed bases are hydrogen bonded to a magenta ribbon lying between the two, labeled "mRNA" by a leader line at its right end and marked 5' at left and 3' at right; its magenta bases read U C A G C U G G C U G A A C G C G U U. Placing the new transcript directly against its template makes the base-by-base complementarity readable in one glance, and comparing it upward with the blue-violet strand shows the two agree except that U stands wherever the sense strand carries T.

interactions.label: Transcription position
interactions.teaches: The antisense strand is read from 3' to 5' while the RNA product grows 5' to 3', adding one complementary ribonucleotide at a time

interactions.label: Base-pairing view
interactions.teaches: Different pair highlights separate template complementarity from the final sequence match: mRNA pairs with antisense DNA, and matches the sense strand except U replaces T
Each base belongs to a directional strand and has a specific partner: DNA A pairs with RNA U, DNA T pairs with RNA A, and C pairs with G

demo_steps.title: Start at the template
demo_steps.narration: At position 0, the transcript has not yet been built. The antisense strand is the template to be read from its 3' end toward its 5' end.

demo_steps.title: Elongation through the bubble
demo_steps.narration: Move to the middle of the gene. The magenta mRNA has grown left-to-right, and each new RNA base is complementary to the cyan antisense base directly below it.

demo_steps.title: Compare transcript with the sense strand
demo_steps.narration: At the full length, switch to the comparison view. The magenta RNA sequence matches the blue-violet sense sequence position by position, except RNA uses U where DNA has T.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Flat 2D schematic in the XY plane with tiny Z offsets only for layering. Overall span about X = -6.3 to +6.3 and Y = -2.2 to +2.1. +X is screen-right, +Y is screen-up. Base spacing in the central bubble is 0.45 world units, with the 19 bubble positions centered from x = -4.05 to +4.05. Three closed DNA-DNA pairs sit to the left at x about -5.85, -5.40, -4.95 and three to the right at x about +4.95, +5.40, +5.85. At the source-like final state, the top sense ribbon is horizontal at y = +1.45 across the bubble, bends downward near x = +/-4.55, and continues as straight outside arms at y = +0.85. The bottom antisense ribbon is horizontal at y = -1.45 across the bubble, bends upward near x = +/-4.55, and continues as straight outside arms at y = -0.85. The magenta mRNA ribbon is a straight horizontal rounded bar at y = +0.20 from x = -4.15 to x = +4.20. Ribbon thickness about 0.23 units with rounded caps and darker stroked edges. Top sense bases hang downward from the upper ribbon: stems from y = +1.33 to +1.08 and letters centered near y = +0.88. mRNA bases hang downward from the magenta ribbon: stems from y = +0.08 to -0.17 and letters centered near y = -0.35. Antisense bubble bases rise upward from the lower ribbon: stems from y = -1.33 to -1.08 and letters centered near y = -0.84. Dotted RNA-DNA hydrogen-bond columns run vertically between mRNA letters and antisense letters, centered near y = -0.58. Closed DNA-DNA hydrogen-bond columns at the far left and right run between the upper and lower outside arms. Left closed pairs shown top-to-bottom: C-G, A-T, T-A. Right closed pairs shown top-to-bottom: G-C, A-T, C-G. Central sense sequence is TCAGCTGGCTGAACGCGTT. Central antisense template sequence is AGTCGACCGACTTGCGCAA. Central mRNA sequence is UCAGCUGGCUGAACGCGUU. Use colors: sense ribbon fill #6f8dca with darker edge #2f63b0 and pale highlight #b9c7e5; antisense ribbon fill #24c6e8 with darker edge #009ed0 and pale highlight #90e5f2; mRNA ribbon fill #ec4aa3 with edge #e2188a and pale highlight #f7acd0. DNA and antisense letters are black #111111; mRNA letters and its 5'/3' labels are magenta #ff0090. Hydrogen-bond dots are black. Leader lines are black thin strokes. On the transcription slider, position n means show the first n mRNA bases from the left; place the active highlight at base index n or n-1, and smoothly open the DNA bubble around the active region while leaving untranscribed bases capable of DNA-DNA pairing. At n = 19, the layout should match the provided source figure with the full central RNA strand visible.
interactionPlan.notes: Render the ribbons as thick extruded or stroked 2D paths with bevelled/rounded joins, not as separate rectangles. Keep the diagram essentially orthographic/front-on with no orbit control. For the base-pairing toggle, reuse the same geometry and change emphasis: DNA-DNA pairs highlights closed duplex dot columns; DNA-RNA pairs highlights the magenta-to-cyan template bonds; Sense-vs-mRNA comparison dims the template bonds and draws translucent vertical guides between the upper sense bases and corresponding RNA bases, using a distinct highlight for T-to-U substitutions. Hover targets should include every visible base letter and its short stem; tooltip text should include strand name, 5'/3' direction, base index, and partner base. Use instanced text sprites or SDF text so the base letters remain crisp in the PDF reader viewport.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for transcription position: drag along the DNA template, and the open bubble advances while the magenta mRNA strand grows 5' to 3' with each new complementary base, showing how the antisense strand directs RNA synthesis.
- Toggle between base-pairing views: switch among DNA-DNA pairs, DNA-RNA pairs, and sense-vs-mRNA comparison, and the relevant hydrogen bonds or matching letters highlight, making complementarity and the T-to-U substitution clear.

authoredContext:
Following formation of the polymerase–promoter complex, several turns of the DNA double helix untwist, forming a bubble and exposing 14 or so base pairs of the two strands. Appropriate ribonucleotides then line up by hydrogen-bonding to their complementary bases on DNA, bond formation occurs in the 5′ → 3′ direction, the RNA polymerase moves along the DNA chain, and the growing RNA molecule unwinds from DNA (the figure). At any one time, about 12 base pairs of the growing RNA remain hydrogen-bonded to the DNA template.

Biosynthesis of RNA using a DNA segment as a template.

Several turns of deoxyribonucleic acid double helix unwind exposing bases of the two strands. Ribonucleotides line up such that hydrogen bonds form in 5-prime to 3-prime direction.

Unlike what happens in DNA replication, where both strands are copied, only one of the two DNA strands is transcribed into mRNA. The DNA strand that contains the gene is often called the sense strand, or coding strand, and the DNA strand that gets transcribed to give RNA is called the antisense strand, or noncoding strand. Because the sense strand and the antisense strand in DNA are complementary, and because the DNA antisense strand and the newly formed RNA strand are also complementary, the RNA molecule produced during transcription is a copy of the DNA sense strand. That is, the complement of the complement is the same as the original. The only difference is that the RNA molecule has a U everywhere that the DNA sense strand has a T.

discrepancies: A yellow active-transcription highlight is visible over the final base, which is not present in the source figure.
The opened DNA bubble is drawn as a more rounded, arched loop, whereas the source has straighter, flatter horizontal central strand segments with sharper side bends.
The generated composition is more vertically compressed in the central region than the source, making the bases and hydrogen-bond dots feel crowded.
The mRNA label and right-side 3′/5′ end labels are more crowded than in the source, reducing the clean separation of the right-side annotations.
The source is a static textbook diagram, while the generated default view includes an instructional control panel and progressive-transcription state that visually changes the figure context.
evaluation.notes: The generated figure is clearly recognizable and conceptually accurate, with good strand colors, sequences, labels, and interactions, but the default highlight and slightly rounded/compressed geometry reduce fidelity to the source.
action_items: Hide the yellow active-base highlight by default or make it optional so the default view matches the source figure.
Straighten and flatten the central opened DNA strands to better match the rectangular transcription bubble shape in the reference.
Increase spacing around the right-side mRNA, 3′, and 5′ labels to better match the clean annotation layout of the source.
Slightly expand the vertical spacing between mRNA and antisense bases to reduce crowding of letters and hydrogen-bond dots.
